hero.title: Incident Taxonomy & Transparency Framework
hero.subtitle: 42 incident types across 6 categories, scored by two levels of metrics and three AI models.

ACC.name: Account Access
ACC.desc: Suspensions, blocks, lockouts, deletions and other restrictions on a user's ability to access their own account.

DAT.name: Data & Privacy
DAT.desc: Breaches, unlawful processing, GDPR violations, undisclosed AI training and other data-handling failures.

FIN.name: Financial
FIN.desc: Unauthorized charges, refund refusals, billing errors, subscription traps and frozen funds.

SUP.name: Support
SUP.desc: Unresponsive support, bot loops with no human escalation, misinformation and language barriers.

CON.name: Content & Service
CON.desc: Arbitrary moderation, undisclosed ToS changes, missing features, downtime and regional restrictions.

AI.name: AI-Specific
AI.desc: Bias, hallucinations causing harm, undisclosed AI identity, automated decisions without appeal and safety failures.

metricsL1.title: Level 1 — Universal Metrics
metricsL1.subtitle: Seven metrics applied to every incident, regardless of category.

M1.name: Terms of Service Clarity
M1.desc: Are the relevant ToS clauses written in plain, unambiguous language accessible to a non-lawyer user?

M2.name: Prior Notification
M2.desc: Was the user notified in advance about the action, change or risk that led to the incident?

M3.name: Explicit Motivation
M3.desc: Did the company provide a specific, verifiable reason rather than a generic policy reference?

M4.name: Appeal Process
M4.desc: Is there a documented, reachable appeal channel with defined steps and timelines?

M5.name: Response Time
M5.desc: How fast did the company acknowledge and substantively address the incident?

M6.name: Data / Money Restitution
M6.desc: Were lost data, access or funds restored to the user when applicable?

M7.name: Public Precedent
M7.desc: Is there a documented public precedent (court ruling, regulator decision, journalistic record) for similar cases?

metricsL2.title: Level 2 — Contextual Metrics
metricsL2.subtitle: Additional metrics activated automatically based on the incident type (e.g. AI explainability for AI-06, GDPR articles for DAT-02).
metricsL2.note: Level 2 metrics are weighted lower than Level 1 in the composite score and serve to refine, not replace, the universal evaluation.

western.name: Western AI
western.desc: Represents the perspective of large US-based commercial AI models trained predominantly on Western-aligned data and policy.

asian.name: Asian AI
asian.desc: Represents the perspective of leading Asian commercial AI models, offering a contrasting cultural and regulatory framing.

opensource.name: Open Source AI
opensource.desc: Represents the perspective of community-auditable open-weight models, used as an independent control.

models.weightNote: The composite score weights the three models equally (1/3 each). Divergences between models are surfaced explicitly rather than averaged away.

score.compositeDesc: Weighted average across the three AI models and the two metric levels for every analyzed incident.
score.scoreNote: SIMULATED — scores are based on public information, not live API connectors.
